supplier_concentration.note: The RHP discloses NO supplier, vendor or raw-material concentration, and none is applicable — the issuer buys no inputs for production. This is an absence of the concept, not an extraction gap: a full-document search finds no procurement, purchase or supplier-concentration table. business_ops.supply_chain_integration: There is no physical supply chain; the relevant integration is vertical integration of the fund-management value chain and full capture of fund economics into the listed entity. (1) Economic integration: 'All the income generated from the funds managed and advised by us, across the three income streams, is received in its entirety by us. Our objective has been to capture the economic value generated by the funds managed and advised by us within our Company, with the goal of enhancing our enterprise value and strengthening our balance sheet.' No Carried Interest is allocated to any individual — 'all the Carried Interest generated across our Gaja Capital Funds is attributable to our Company without any specific allocation to any individual'. (2) Structural integration: the Company acts as investment manager to the India-domiciled AIF constituents while its own subsidiary Gaja Advisors Ltd, Mauritius acts as investment manager to the Mauritius-domiciled constituent funds, and Eastgate Secondaries Advisor LLP (in which the Company holds an investment) will manage the proposed Secondaries Fund; operations run through seven subsidiaries (four Indian, one overseas, two overseas step-down). (3) Backward integration into distribution (fund-raising): 'We have traditionally relied on our network of investors to raise funds for the Gaja Capital Funds while keeping the proportion of funds raised through third-party distributors low' — three distributors used in Fiscal 2024 and none in Fiscal 2025 or Fiscal 2026. (4) Balance-sheet integration into the funds: sponsor commitments substantially above the SEBI AIF Regulations threshold (Rs 2,740.00 million, 6.41% of total fund size as of March 31, 2026, against a prescribed 2.5% of corpus or Rs 50.00 million, whichever is lower), the past warehousing of an investment in a portfolio company for Fund IV on the Company's own balance sheet, and investment of balance-sheet capital in third-party funds to bolster deal flow. Cells printed as a dash were treated as not printed and omitted rather than recorded as zero. Figures printed in brackets are reproduced as negatives. record_gaps: Fiscal 2024 - audit trail (edit log) absent for the whole year: with effect from April 01, 2023 the Company should have used accounting software having the audit trail (edit log) feature throughout the year for all relevant transactions; however the Company used accounting software that did not have such features, and the auditor was unable to comment on the audit trail feature of the said software at the time of finalisation of the statutory audit for the financial year ended March 31, 2024 (described in Note 43 of the standalone financial statements).

Fiscal 2025 - audit trail (edit log) absent for the whole year: the same adverse remark is repeated; the Company used accounting software for maintaining its books of account which did not have a feature of recording audit trail (edit log) facility throughout the year for all relevant transactions, and the auditor was unable to comment on the audit trail feature of the said software (described in Note 41 of the standalone financial statements).

Fiscal 2026 - audit trail (edit log) gap of approximately five months: the accounting software has the audit trail feature and it operated throughout the year for all the relevant transactions recorded in the software EXCEPT for the period from April 01, 2025 to August 27, 2025 where the feature was not enabled. The audit trail has been preserved as per statutory requirements for record retention only from the date of enablement of the audit trail, except for the period where the audit trail feature was not enabled (described in Note 41 of the standalone financial statements). Corrective measure stated: an accounting software with an audit trail feature was fully implemented with effect from August 28, 2025.

Books of account qualified for Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026: the auditors report states that in their opinion proper books of account as required by law have been kept by the Company so far as it appears from their examination of those books EXCEPT for the matters stated in the Rule 11(g) reporting paragraphs (paragraph 14(h)(vi) for FY2024, paragraph 17(g)(v) for FY2025 and paragraph 16(h)(vi) for FY2026), with a corresponding modification relating to the maintenance of accounts and other matters connected therewith reported under Section 143(3)(b) of the Companies Act, 2013.

Form CRL-1 not filed: the Registrar of Companies, NCT of Delhi and Haryana issued a notice dated May 31, 2018 in relation to non-filing of Form CRL-1 under Rule 4(i) of the Companies (Restriction on Number of Layers) Rules, 2017. The Company replied that the form was not required as it does not have more than two layers of subsidiaries. No communication has been received from the RoC since the response was submitted, so the matter remains formally unclosed on the record as of the date of the RHP.

Form FC-GPR filed late with the RBI for the bonus issue dated June 7, 2025 and the preferential allotment dated June 13, 2025; late submission fees of INR 14,500 and INR 21,600 respectively were paid.

One member of the Promoter Group, Mr. Johrilal Jain, has not provided his consent to be identified as a member of the Promoter Group (heading of Risk Factor 10). overview.business_model: The Company states it derives income primarily from three streams: (i) Management Fee - the fee received for providing management and advisory services to funds, a function of the size of a fund and applicable on capital committed/invested by external investors; (ii) Carried Interest - the performance-linked share of profits generated by the funds managed and advised by it, a function of the respective funds' net IRR, calculated on a fund as a whole and not investment-by-investment; and (iii) Income from Sponsor Commitment - capital gains earned on its own capital commitment as sponsor to the funds, a function of the gross MOIC of a fund. All income generated by the funds across the three streams is received in its entirety by the Company. On the expenditure side, team compensation forms a substantial share of expenses, with fund-raise and business development costs the other major items. The RHP expressly cautions that after Allotment, investors will be shareholders of the AMC entity and not investors in the funds, and shall not receive returns, distributions or profits from fund performance except to the extent of dividends declared by the Company from its own profits. The largest uses of the Fresh Issue fund vehicles that do not yet hold capital: ₹2,100.00 million of Sponsor Commitment is earmarked for proposed Fund V, whose private placement memorandum application was filed with SEBI on June 10, 2026 and remains pending, and ₹1,050.00 million for the Secondaries Fund, registered as a Category II AIF on October 17, 2025 but with no capital raised; the RHP states 'None of the Objects for which the Net Proceeds will be utilized have been appraised by any bank, financial institution or agency.'

Related-party transactions run at 102.76%, 113.74% and 106.00% of total income in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 (₹1,621.57 million, ₹1,402.44 million and ₹1,101.96 million against total income of ₹1,577.97 million, ₹1,233.07 million and ₹1,039.60 million) — the counterparties are the company's own funds and affiliates, so essentially the whole profit and loss account is transacted inside the group.

The recurring fee line has gone backwards while carry filled the gap: advisory fees were ₹758.54 million in FY2024, ₹575.23 million in FY2025 and ₹600.80 million in FY2026, and Management Fee fell from 72.96% of total income in FY2024 to 38.07% in FY2026; the RHP's own fund-raising table prints total funds raised as Nil for both Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025 against ₹4,705.70 million in Fiscal 2024, noting no funds other than Fund IV were raised in the period. Income-generating Capital has declined for two straight years: ₹32,659.3 million (FY2024), ₹32,375.97 million (FY2025), ₹31,617.76 million (FY2026).

FY2026 other income of ₹222.66 million against ₹13.08 million in FY2025 is dominated by a non-cash item: ₹167.43 million is a fair-value change on investments measured at FVTPL in the company's own funds, recognised in profit after tax but stripped out of the RHP's own EBITDA definition, which expressly reduces other income.

The operating base is very small for the capital being raised: 23 permanent employees as of March 31, 2026 (37 personnel in total including 14 contractual), of whom the Core Team is 15; Risk Factor 22 states high dependence on the Promoters, KMP and Senior Management, and total employee attrition was 13.33% in FY2026.

Governance-record items cluster around the promoter group: SEBI rejected by letter dated September 23, 2025 the company's application for exemption from disclosing details of Promoter Group member Mr. Johrilal Jain, who has not responded to any correspondence, so his disclosures rest only on public-domain sources; and Gaja Capital India Fund - I settled with SEBI under the VCF Settlement Scheme 2025 for ₹500,000.00 by order dated March 9, 2026.

Returns sit at the bottom of the disclosed comparison set: RoNW of 13.13% for FY2026 is down from 15.31% in FY2025 and is the second-lowest in the RHP's own peer table, above only UTI Asset Management Company Limited at 8.97%, while peers such as ICICI Prudential AMC (79.07%), SBI Funds Management (51.44%) and Anand Rathi Wealth (39.64%) print far higher.

The disclosed peer group is not like-for-like and the RHP says why: the nine listed peers are mutual-fund AMCs and wealth managers with revenue from operations of ₹11,488.25 million to ₹57,646.30 million against the issuer's ₹1,355.31 million, because the Crisil Report records 'No listed AIFs' in India — a comparability limitation the document itself discloses rather than an extraction gap.

Part of the consolidated financials was not audited by the principal auditor: subsidiaries whose share of the restated consolidated totals is printed as total assets ₹2,722.31 million and revenue ₹1,053.46 million for FY2026 were audited by other auditors, in a group where the Mauritius segment produced ₹1,030.53 million of FY2026 external revenue against India's ₹324.78 million.

Selling shareholders exit from a near-zero cost base: certified average cost of acquisition per Equity Share is ₹0.00 for Ms. Sudesh Jain and Mr. Anshuman Goyal, ₹0.10 for Mr. Ranjit Jayant Shah and Ms. Suparna Kumar, ₹0.12 for Mr. Sanjay Hiralal Patel, ₹7.28 for Mr. Imran Jafar, ₹11.66 for Mr. Abhinav Jain and ₹20.58 for Mr. Sushane Chopra, with the weighted average cost of acquisition for both the last one year and the last three years certified as 'Nil'.

Three Mauritius approvals held by Material Subsidiary Gaja Advisors Ltd — the global business licence, the investment adviser (restricted) licence and the tax residence certificate — have been applied for renewal but not obtained, two of them stated to be 'Subject to settlement of the renewal fees', in the entity through which the offshore revenue arises.

Contingent items are disclosed but partly unquantified: a carried-interest liability of Gaja Advisors Ltd (Mauritius) to certain fund investors estimated at ₹126.59 million at March 31, 2026 (₹154.00 million prior year); a Mauritius Revenue Authority demand of USD 153,563 (₹14.54 million) under appeal with 10% deposited under protest; a corporate guarantee by Gaja Corporate Advisors Private Limited to 360 One for a loan of the holding company with no amount printed; and a Fund IV clawback obligation (Risk Factor 14) with no quantum stated anywhere.
data_gaps: No Price Band, Floor Price, Cap Price or Offer Price is printed anywhere in this RHP — every price-dependent cell is [●], to be completed prior to filing of the Prospectus with the RoC.

The issuer's own P/E is printed 'N.A.' and its closing price 'NA'; the P/E on basic and diluted EPS at both ends of the Price Band, the market capitalisation to revenue multiple for Fiscals 2026 and 2025, and the enterprise value to EBITDA ratio are all [●].

The number of Equity Shares in the Fresh Issue, in the Offer for Sale and in the total Offer is not printed; nor is post-Offer paid-up capital, post-Offer securities premium, the post-Offer promoter percentage or any dilution percentage.

Net Proceeds are not stated (Gross Proceeds of ₹4,500.00 million less Offer-related expenses, both to be finalised); every line of the Offer Expenses table including the total is [●]; the general corporate purposes amount and the Total row of the deployment schedule are [●], with only the 25% of Gross Proceeds cap printed.

No AUM or fee-paying AUM is printed for the issuer — 'AUM' appears in the RHP only for the Indian alternatives industry as a whole (Crisil Report); the issuer's own capital metric is 'Income-generating Capital'.
No EBITDA margin is computed anywhere in the document, and no ROCE, return on capital employed or capital employed figure appears in the RHP in any form.

No working-capital metrics are printed for any year — no debtor days, creditor days, inventory days or cash conversion cycle; the only related disclosure is the qualitative statement that receivables mature within 0-60 days and payables terms are approximately 0-90 days.
No trade receivables ageing schedule and no trade payables ageing schedule exist in the RHP; the only ageing schedule in the document is for capital work-in-progress at Note 6.2.
No ISIN is printed for the Equity Shares anywhere in the document.

No aggregate amount is printed for proceedings against the Promoters (the column reads '-' for four disclosed proceedings), no aggregate contingent-liability figure is printed, no amount is stated for the corporate guarantee given by Gaja Corporate Advisors Private Limited to 360 One, and no clawback quantum is stated for Fund IV.

No reserves, sales, profit after tax, EPS, diluted EPS or net asset value is printed for any of the eleven Group Companies — the RHP states this information is hosted on the company website and expressly does not form part of the RHP.
The Company and its Subsidiaries have obtained no credit ratings as of the RHP date, so no external rating opinion on the borrowings is available in the document.

No calendar expiry date is printed for any lock-in tranche (periods only), and every cell of the minimum promoters' contribution table — shares locked in, dates, acquisition price, percentage of pre- and post-Offer capital — is [●].

Post-Offer NAV per Equity Share at Floor, Cap and Offer Price is 'to be computed after finalisation of the Price Band'; no target fund size is printed for the proposed Fund V or the Secondaries Fund other than Board-approved capital-commitment intentions, and neither has raised capital.

Separately from what the document withholds, two items were lost or limited in our own extraction rather than by the RHP: the name cell of the allottee of 347,343 Equity Shares in the June 13, 2025 preferential allotment did not survive PDF text extraction (a Capital Structure footnote indicates the HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited - Shareholders Solvency Margin Account), and the registered-office address of Group Company GPE (India) Ltd is truncated mid-line in the extracted Group Companies table.

Progress of FIR No. 0150 against the Promoters and Gaja Trustee Company Private Limited, and enforcement of the SIAC award of January 7, 2021 (aggregate ₹1,546.32 million printed for the row) through the Enforcement Petition of February 21, 2022 before the High Court of Madras.

open_questions: How much of the ₹682.55 million carried interest recognised from Gaja Capital Fund I Ltd in FY2026 has been received in cash, given the ₹1,045.46 million related-party receivable from Gaja Capital India Fund I standing at March 31, 2026 against nil at March 31, 2025?

Fund II is described as 'deployed and largely realized' as of March 31, 2026 — what quantum of carried interest remains attributable to it, and from which fund does the carry line come once Fund II is fully realised?

The RHP prints total funds raised as Nil for Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025 — what is the expected first-close date and Management Fee rate for Fund V, whose SEBI private placement memorandum application of June 10, 2026 was still pending at the RHP date?

Income-generating Capital, the company's own capital-base metric, declined from ₹32,659.3 million (FY2024) to ₹32,375.97 million (FY2025) to ₹31,617.76 million (FY2026) — what drives the decline, and how does it reconcile with the stated intent to 'raise larger funds'?

The Fund IV clawback obligation (Risk Factor 14) is unquantified — what is the maximum amount of previously received Carried Interest that could be required to be returned, and under what preferred-return shortfall?

Note 17 shows a non-current term loan from 360 One Prime Limited of ₹67.80 million at March 31, 2026 while the June 30, 2026 Financial Indebtedness statement shows ₹9.58 million for the same lender; the RHP does not explain the movement between the two dates.

The Financial Indebtedness section states an interest-rate range of 10.25% p.a. to 13.00% p.a. that is not consistent with the facility-level rates printed in the same chapter and in Note 17 (vehicle loans 9.50%-10.25%, ICICI overdraft 7.25% and 7.85% on the enhanced limit) — which range governs?

Note 25 prints interest income on income tax refund of ₹2.74 million for FY2024, but the Restated Consolidated Cash Flow Statement shows '-' for that line in FY2024; the two statements do not agree and the RHP does not reconcile them.

The RHP prints two different definitions of RoNW while quoting the same 13.13% figure — 'PAT as a percentage of average Net Worth' in Other Financial Information versus 'restated net worth at the end of the year' in Basis for Offer Price; which basis underpins the peer-table comparison?

What amount is guaranteed under the corporate guarantee given by Gaja Corporate Advisors Private Limited to 360 One for a loan availed by the holding company — the item is disclosed as a contingent liability with no figure printed?

Note 37 records that a recoverable balance of ₹55.28 million was reclassified during FY2026 from Shree Capital Advisors, LLC to the proposed Secondaries Fund (Mauritius) 'based on management's revised assessment of the expected recovery counterparty' — what underlies the change of counterparty?
verdict.our_read: Gaja Alternative Asset Management is the listed manager of the 20-year-old Gaja Capital mid-market private-equity franchise — the Offer conveys ownership of the fee-and-carry entity, not of the funds — and the make-or-break tension is that carried interest of ₹682.55 million from a single 2007-vintage fund, Gaja Capital Fund I Ltd, was 50.36% of FY2026 revenue from operations while cash from operations was negative ₹149.82 million, and the two largest components of the ₹3,720.00 million object (₹2,100.00 million to Fund V and ₹1,050.00 million to the Secondaries Fund) are sponsor commitments to funds that have not yet raised any capital.

SEBI VCF Settlement Scheme order dated March 9, 2026 requiring ₹500,000.00 from Gaja Capital India Fund - I; pending FIR No. 0150 naming Promoters Mr. Gopal Jain and Mr. Imran Jafar and Subsidiary Gaja Trustee Company Private Limited; FC-GPR late fees of ₹14,500 and ₹21,600; three unrenewed Mauritius approvals; all six 'Gaja' trademarks applied for December 4, 2024 and none registered.

red_flags: The statutory auditors carried an adverse remark on the audit trail (edit log) in all three fiscals, with a corresponding modification on maintenance of proper books of account under Section 143(3)(b): in Fiscals 2024 and 2025 the accounting software had no audit-trail feature at all and the auditors were 'unable to comment' on it, and in Fiscal 2026 the feature was not enabled from April 01, 2025 to August 27, 2025. The company states replacement software with the feature was fully implemented from August 28, 2025 and that there is no instance of the audit trail being tampered with where the feature was enabled — but for two full years and five further months there was no edit log to examine.

Related-party transactions equalled 102.76%, 113.74% and 106.00% of total income in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 — ₹1,621.57 million, ₹1,402.44 million and ₹1,101.96 million against total income of ₹1,577.97 million, ₹1,233.07 million and ₹1,039.60 million. The RHP explains the ratio exceeds 100% because both income and expense transactions are included, and Nangia & Co. LLP certified compliance with applicable laws (certificate dated August 12, 2026, UDIN 26076879DDPOPZ6634); the counterparties are nonetheless the issuer's own funds, subsidiaries and directors, and the FY2026 balance includes a ₹1,045.46 million receivable from Gaja Capital India Fund I that was nil a year earlier.

A bonus issue of 104,160,000 Equity Shares in the ratio of 2,500 for every 1 share held was allotted on June 7, 2025 — fourteen months before this RHP dated August 12, 2026 and inside the 18-month window — following a sub-division of face value from ₹10 to ₹5 on March 3, 2025; ₹419.80 million of retained earnings and ₹100.99 million of securities premium were separately debited for it, the FY2025 auditor's emphasis of matter notes EPS was recalculated for the bonus 'despite it being a post facto event', and the certified weighted average cost of acquisition for the Promoters and Selling Shareholders is 'Nil' for both the last one year and the last three years.

Promoters Mr. Gopal Jain and Mr. Imran Jafar, together with Subsidiary Gaja Trustee Company Private Limited and others, are respondents to criminal proceedings under FIR No. 0150 invoking sections 403, 405, 415, 418, 420 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, filed by Mr. Harjeet Singh on behalf of Educomp Learning Private Limited over investments in EuroKids International Private Limited, a Fund II portfolio company, and registered pursuant to a court order dated July 6, 2022; the High Court by orders dated October 5, 2023 and October 19, 2023 directed that no coercive steps be taken against the petitioners, and the matters remain pending. The RHP prints no aggregate amount for proceedings against the Promoters.

Promoter Group member Mr. Johrilal Jain, father of Promoter Mr. Gopal Jain, has not consented to be identified and has provided no information or certifications, with all correspondence unanswered; the company's application under Regulation 300(1)(c) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations for exemption from disclosing his details and those of his relevant entities was rejected by SEBI by letter dated September 23, 2025, so disclosures about him rest only on publicly available sources and the company states it cannot identify an exhaustive list of his relevant entities.

The name of Promoter Mr. Gopal Jain appears in the RBI list of 'defaults above Rs. 1 crore under Non-Suit Filed Accounts' through his erstwhile nominee/non-executive directorship at Educomp Infrastructure and School Management Limited from April 5, 2008 to February 5, 2013. The RHP states in the same disclosure that this list is separate from the Wilful Defaulters list, that his name does not appear on the Wilful Defaulters list, that he was not associated with the entity at the time of the defaults, that a TransUnion CIBIL search shows his name is not in the suit-filed defaults list, and that a communication has been received from Union Bank of India regarding removal of his name from the suit filed list; the residual risk of adverse action is retained as a risk factor and no default amount is quantified anywhere.

Gaja Capital India Fund - I, a fund managed and advised by the company, settled with SEBI under the VCF Settlement Scheme 2025 for non-compliance with Regulations 23(1) and 17(1) of the erstwhile SEBI (Venture Capital Funds) Regulations, 1996, paying ₹500,000.00 pursuant to an order dated March 9, 2026 — five months before this RHP.

Both mid-2025 share issuances were reported late to the RBI: Form FC-GPR was filed late for the bonus issue of June 7, 2025 and the preferential allotment of June 13, 2025, with late submission fees of ₹14,500 and ₹21,600 respectively paid to the RBI.

The regulated entity carrying the offshore revenue is operating on lapsed-and-renewed approvals: Material Subsidiary Gaja Advisors Ltd, Mauritius holds a global business licence and an investment adviser (restricted) licence each valid only to June 30, 2026 and a tax residence certificate valid to June 11, 2026, all three with renewals 'applied for but not yet obtained' at the RHP date and two 'Subject to settlement of the renewal fees' — against Mauritius segment revenue of ₹1,030.53 million in FY2026.

None of the six 'Gaja' trademarks — including 'Gaja Capital' (application 6741259) and 'Gaja Capital Partners' (6741260), all applied for on December 4, 2024 — is registered as of the RHP date, in a business whose principal asset the document repeatedly describes as its brand and reputation.
strengths_observed: The entire fund economics land in the listed entity: the RHP states all income from Management Fee, Carried Interest and Income from Sponsor Commitment is 'received in its entirety by us' and that 'all the Carried Interest generated across our Gaja Capital Funds is attributable to our Company without any specific allocation to any individual' — a structure that produced profit after tax of ₹819.59 million (FY2026), ₹619.51 million (FY2025) and ₹447.42 million (FY2024), a CAGR the RHP prints as 35.34%.

Auditor-certified balance sheet with little leverage and no promoter pledge: net worth ₹6,065.15 million at March 31, 2026 against ₹3,318.77 million at March 31, 2024; total borrowings ₹415.56 million at March 31, 2026 (₹606.97 million at June 30, 2026, of which the ₹582.27 million ICICI Bank overdraft is secured against fixed deposits); cash and cash equivalents ₹710.74 million; the RHP states 'none of the Equity Shares held by our Promoters are pledged'.

Fund-level performance is printed rather than asserted, as of March 31, 2026: Fund II (2007) MOIC 3.81x, TVPI 2.41x, IRR 18.61%, loss ratio 13.81%; Fund III (2015) MOIC 1.88x, TVPI 1.53x and IRR 9.40% (both stated 1st quartile), loss ratio 19.17%; Fund IV (2021) TVPI 1.47x and IRR 27.91% (both 1st quartile, unrealised, 62.00% of capital deployed); Prior Investments of ₹210.93 million fully realized at 5.61x.

Sponsor capital well above the regulatory floor: aggregate Sponsor Commitment of approximately ₹2,740.00 million, 6.41% of the total size of the Gaja Capital Funds, against the SEBI AIF Regulations requirement of 2.5% of corpus or ₹50.00 million whichever is lower; fair market value of those commitments ₹2,436.23 million at March 31, 2026 (₹2,015.42 million FY2025).

Institutional capital came in pre-Offer at a struck price: preferential allotment of 8,683,566 Equity Shares on June 13, 2025 at ₹143.95 per share aggregating approximately ₹1,250.00 million, taken up by HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited (3,473,428 shares held, 3.08%), SBI Life Insurance Company Limited (1,736,705, 1.54%) and Wealthwave Capital Incorporated VCC Sub-Fund I (1,180,967, 1.05%).

Distribution is largely proprietary and the investor base is broad: 298 Limited Partners as of March 31, 2026 (139 in India, 159 outside India) spread across more than 20 countries, with 63.42% of total capital commitments raised outside India; three third-party distributors were used in Fiscal 2024 and none in Fiscal 2025 or Fiscal 2026.

Board and retention record: nine directors including former SEBI chairman Mr. Upendra Kumar Sinha as Non-Executive Chairman, Mr. Arindam Kumar Bhattacharya chairing the Audit Committee and Mr. Shailesh Vishnubhai Haribhakti chairing the Nomination and Remuneration Committee; the RHP prints attrition of Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management as nil in each of Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
